# Tasks

## 1. Worktree

- [ ] 1.1 Create the task worktree from the primary checkout with `git worktree add .worktrees/widget-cache -b widget-cache main` and move the session into it; every later task runs there. Verify: `test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = widget-cache && test "$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")" = widget-cache`

## 2. Memoized widget lookup

- [ ] 2.1 Add `src/cache.test.ts` (`bun:test`, imports `getWidget` from `./cache`) with exactly three tests, each using ids no other test uses: (1) the returned widget equals `{ id }` and is a plain object for `"t1-a"`, `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"` and `""` (requirement "Widget lookup returns a widget carrying the requested id"); (2) two lookups of `"t2-a"` are `Object.is`-identical and a property added to the first is visible on the second (requirement "Repeated lookups of one id return the same widget instance"); (3) looking up `"t3-a"`, `"t3-b"`, `"t3-a"` yields identical `"t3-a"` results and a different `"t3-b"` result with `id` `"t3-b"` (requirement "Distinct ids return distinct widget instances"). Run it against the unchanged `src/cache.ts` to record RED: test 1 passes and tests 2 and 3 fail, because the current code builds a new object per call. Verify: `out=$(bun test src/cache.test.ts 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qx ' 1 pass' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qx ' 2 fail'`
- [ ] 2.2 In `src/cache.ts`, add a module-private `Map<string, { id: string }>` and make `getWidget` return the stored widget for a known id, otherwise create `{ id }`, store it and return it; keep the exported signature and add no export. Commit `src/cache.ts` and `src/cache.test.ts` by explicit path. Verify: `out=$(bun test src/cache.test.ts 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qx ' 3 pass' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qx ' 0 fail' && git diff --quiet HEAD -- src && test "$(grep -c '^export' src/cache.ts)" = 1`

## 3. Final verification

- [ ] 3.1 F1. Manual QA on the real surface: merge the default branch (`main`) into the work branch when it is not an ancestor of the head, and commit; then run the six `standard` QA rows below, each a `bun -e` script that imports `getWidget` from `./src/cache.ts`, prints every call it makes with its result and the comparisons it checks, and whose stdout is saved as the row's evidence. Rows and the observation each must show: `r1-requested-id.txt` (requirement 1: widgets for `"a"`, `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"`, `""` print as `{"id":<same id>}`); `r2-same-instance.txt` (requirement 2: `Object.is` of two `"a"` lookups prints `true`, and a property set on the first appears on the second); `r3-distinct-ids.txt` (requirement 3: after `"a"`, `"b"`, `"a"`, the `"a"` identity prints `true`, `"a"` vs `"b"` identity prints `false`, the `"b"` id prints `b`); `happy-path.txt` (one lookup of `"widget-1"` prints `{"id":"widget-1"}`); `edge-prototype-keys.txt` (riskiest edge: `"__proto__"` and `"constructor"` lookups each print an own `id` property equal to the key and `Object.getPrototypeOf` equal to `Object.prototype`, and a repeat lookup of each is identical); `regression-shape.txt` (adjacent behaviour: `JSON.stringify(getWidget("x"))` prints exactly `{"id":"x"}` and `Object.keys` prints `["id"]`, as before the change). One evidence path per row in `.omp/team-config/evidence/gate/widget-cache/f1/`, on the head after the last code commit; the QA lane judges the observations. Verify: `for f in r1-requested-id r2-same-instance r3-distinct-ids happy-path edge-prototype-keys regression-shape; do test -s ".omp/team-config/evidence/gate/widget-cache/f1/$f.txt" || exit 1; done`

## Workflow follow-up

- F2 merge gate (`review-work`), after 3.1 and never a checkbox: the record binds every file of this folder by `plan_sha256`, tasks.md included, so the folder is final before the F2 snapshot.
- Merge only after the F2 record validates.

# Delegation and Parallel Dispatch (omp)

**Pick the agent by reasoning difficulty, not diff size.** `scout`/`sonic` run on the cheap
`@smol` model: give them only lookups and mechanical edits. A one-line change that needs an
evidence document cross-checked, a serialization format preserved, or git history reasoned
about goes to `task` (or stays with you). `oracle` is for architecture calls and debugging
after two failed attempts; `auditor`/`reviewer` are for finished diffs; `plan-reviewer` for plans and fix deltas.

**Overlapping tasks never run in the same batch.** Derive each item's file-set from the plan's
`Files:` lines or the scope. Items overlap when their sets intersect, including shared barrels,
i18n, tokens, and config. Overlapping items go in separate `task` calls, one after the other;
disjoint items may share a batch. An unknown file-set overlaps everything.
Items that are read-only reviewers over the same committed inputs (the `review-work` gate lanes, the `omp-gated` plan-review scopes) do not overlap and may share a batch; editing items keep this rule.

**Two or more concurrent editing tasks run isolated.** Pass `isolated: true` on the task item
(or enable `task.isolation.enabled`), so each child edits its own APFS clone and its changes
come back as a patch. A real collision then surfaces as a failed apply, not a silent interleave.

**A running subagent owns its files.** Do not edit them until its result arrives (`wait`, or the
delivered `task-result`). A staged-but-uncommitted tree looks the same as finished work.

**Reviews stay small and start fresh.** Split a large review by shared files into 2-3 reviewer
tasks, not one per angle. Put the `file:line` inventory and only the relevant plan excerpt in the
brief; ask for blockers with `file:line`, at most 5 notes, and one verdict line. A re-review
after fixes is a new task with the delta and the open blockers, never a follow-up message to the
old reviewer (`write agent://...`). The review-work TRAILER REPAIR. message is not a re-review: it
goes to the same reviewer by design. A procedure that prescribes its own brief overrides this
paragraph: review-work and integration-review dispatch their verbatim briefs, and the OpenSpec
`omp-gated` review artifact dispatches its fixed brief for every round, with the two paths filled
in and nothing added.

**After every editing subagent:** check `git reflog <default-branch> -3` and `git worktree list`.
Unexpected movement of the default branch is an incident to report.

One option is to make `id` non-writable with `Object.defineProperty`, which keeps the object's identity and any added properties, and leaves `JSON.stringify` and `Object.keys` output unchanged. The catch is that assigning to `id` would now throw a TypeError in strict mode, so that behavior change needs weighing.

I'm looking at the cache-hit options for the `id` problem: either make `id` read-only so assignments throw in strict mode, or reset it on each hit, which would silently undo a caller's change. # Spec Delta

## Purpose

Widget lookup returns one shared widget object per id for the life of the process, so repeated lookups reuse the widget instead of creating a new one.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Widget lookup returns a widget carrying the requested id
Looking up a widget by an id string SHALL return a widget whose `id` equals that string, for every string including the empty string and strings that name JavaScript object-prototype keys.

#### Scenario: Ordinary id
- **WHEN** a caller looks up the widget with id `"a"`
- **THEN** the returned widget's `id` is `"a"`

#### Scenario: Prototype-key ids
- **WHEN** a caller looks up the widgets with ids `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"` and `""`
- **THEN** each returned widget is a plain object whose `id` equals the id it was looked up with

#### Scenario: Negative control
- **WHEN** the cache is keyed by a plain object so that looking up `"__proto__"` or `"constructor"` returns a prototype member instead of a widget
- **THEN** the check that the returned widget's `id` equals the requested id MUST fail

### Requirement: Repeated lookups of one id return the same widget instance
Every lookup of an id after the first SHALL return the identical object returned by the first lookup of that id, for the lifetime of the process.

#### Scenario: Same id twice
- **WHEN** a caller looks up id `"a"` twice
- **THEN** both results are the same object (`Object.is` is true)

#### Scenario: Mutation is shared
- **WHEN** a caller looks up id `"a"`, adds a property to the result, and looks up `"a"` again
- **THEN** the second result carries the added property

#### Scenario: Negative control
- **WHEN** lookup creates a new widget object on every call, as it does before this change
- **THEN** the identity check on two lookups of `"a"` MUST fail

### Requirement: Distinct ids return distinct widget instances
Lookups of two different ids SHALL return two different objects, each carrying its own id, regardless of lookup order.

#### Scenario: Two ids interleaved
- **WHEN** a caller looks up `"a"`, then `"b"`, then `"a"` again
- **THEN** the two `"a"` results are the same object, the `"b"` result is a different object, and its `id` is `"b"`

#### Scenario: Negative control
- **WHEN** the cache stores a single widget regardless of id, so looking up `"b"` after `"a"` returns the `"a"` widget
- **THEN** the check that the `"b"` result differs from the `"a"` result and has `id` `"b"` MUST fail

# Proposal

## Why

`getWidget(id)` in `src/cache.ts` builds a new widget object on every call, so two lookups of the same id yield two distinct objects and the module named `cache` caches nothing. Callers that compare widgets by identity, or that look up the same id repeatedly, get no reuse.

## What Changes

- `getWidget(id)` memoizes its result per id for the lifetime of the process: the first call for an id creates the widget, every later call with the same id returns that same object instance.
- Distinct ids keep yielding distinct widgets, each carrying its own id, including ids that collide with JavaScript object-prototype keys (`__proto__`, `constructor`).
- A widget's `id` becomes read-only: assigning to it throws a `TypeError`, so a caller cannot make the shared cached widget carry another id (user decision). Other properties stay writable and shared.
- The cache is unbounded and has no eviction, expiry or invalidation API (user decision: in-process memoization only).
- The return type becomes `{ readonly id: string }`, matching the runtime read-only id; the parameter, the function name and the set of exports are unchanged.
- A `bun test` suite (`src/cache.test.ts`) is added; the repository has no tests or test runner configuration today.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `widget-cache`: per-id reuse of widget objects returned by widget lookup.

### Modified Capabilities

None (the project has no existing specs).

## Impact

- Code: `src/cache.ts` (only file in `src/`; no in-repo callers of `getWidget`).
- Behaviour visible to callers: repeated calls now return the same object, so a caller's added or changed property (other than `id`) is seen by every later caller of that id; assigning `id` now throws instead of succeeding.
- Memory: one retained entry per distinct id requested, never released while the process runs.
- Tooling: new test file run with the installed `bun` (no `package.json`, no new dependency).

# Design

## Context

`src/cache.ts` exports one function, `getWidget(id: string): { id: string }`, which returns a fresh object literal on every call. The repository has no `package.json`, no dependencies, no tests and no in-repo callers of `getWidget`. Motivation: see proposal.md - Why. Requirements: specs/widget-cache/spec.md.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Memoize `getWidget` per id inside the module, with the exported signature unchanged.

**Non-Goals:**
- Eviction, capacity limits, expiry, invalidation or a reset hook (user decision: unbounded in-process memoization).
- Freezing or copying returned widgets; callers share the cached instance.
- Cross-process or persistent caching.

## Decisions

### Module-private `Map<string, { id: string }>`

`getWidget` looks the id up in a module-level `Map`; on a miss it creates `{ id }`, stores it and returns it; on a hit it returns the stored object.

- Alternative: a plain object (`Record<string, Widget>`). Rejected: ids such as `"__proto__"` and `"constructor"` resolve to `Object.prototype` members, which the first requirement's negative control targets. `Object.create(null)` would avoid that but adds a subtlety a `Map` does not have.
- Alternative: a generic `memoize` helper. Rejected: one call site; a helper adds an abstraction with no second user.
- Alternative: export the `Map` or a `clearWidgetCache()` for tests. Rejected: it widens the public surface beyond the spec. Tests instead use ids unique to each test, so test order cannot leak state between them.

### Build vs. adopt: in-process memoization cache
- Repository: none; searched `src/` (only `src/cache.ts:1-3`, no cache structure), no `package.json` or `node_modules`, so no installed dependency.
- Platform: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Map (built-in `Map`: string-keyed storage with no prototype-key collisions; unbounded memoization needs nothing beyond `get`/`set`).
- Candidates: not searched, covered above
- Decision: adopt the built-in `Map`

### Tests with `bun test`

`src/cache.test.ts` imports `getWidget` from `./cache` and uses `bun:test`. Bun 1.4.4 is installed and runs TypeScript without configuration, so no `package.json` or dependency is added. One test file covers all three requirements.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Unbounded growth: every distinct id stays in memory for the process lifetime] → Accepted by the user's choice of unbounded memoization; recorded in gate.md.
- [Shared mutable instance: one caller's mutation is visible to all later callers of that id] → Specified behaviour (spec scenario "Mutation is shared"); not mitigated by freezing because that would change the returned type's contract.
- [Module state persists across tests in one `bun test` process] → Each test uses ids no other test uses.

# Design

## Context

`src/cache.ts` exports one function, `getWidget(id: string): { id: string }`, which returns a fresh object literal on every call. The repository has no `package.json`, no dependencies, no tests and no in-repo callers of `getWidget`. Motivation: see proposal.md - Why. Requirements: specs/widget-cache/spec.md.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Memoize `getWidget` per id inside the module, with the exported signature unchanged.

**Non-Goals:**
- Eviction, capacity limits, expiry, invalidation or a reset hook (user decision: unbounded in-process memoization).
- Freezing or copying returned widgets; callers share the cached instance.
- Cross-process or persistent caching.

## Decisions

### Module-private `Map<string, { id: string }>`

`getWidget` looks the id up in a module-level `Map`; on a miss it creates `{ id }`, stores it and returns it; on a hit it returns the stored object.

- Alternative: a plain object (`Record<string, Widget>`). Rejected: ids such as `"__proto__"` and `"constructor"` resolve to `Object.prototype` members, which the first requirement's negative control targets. `Object.create(null)` would avoid that but adds a subtlety a `Map` does not have.
- Alternative: a generic `memoize` helper. Rejected: one call site; a helper adds an abstraction with no second user.
- Alternative: export the `Map` or a `clearWidgetCache()` for tests. Rejected: it widens the public surface beyond the spec. Tests instead use ids unique to each test, so test order cannot leak state between them.

### Build vs. adopt: in-process memoization cache
- Repository: none; searched `src/` (only `src/cache.ts:1-3`, no cache structure), no `package.json` or `node_modules`, so no installed dependency.
- Platform: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Map (built-in `Map`: string-keyed storage with no prototype-key collisions; unbounded memoization needs nothing beyond `get`/`set`).
- Candidates: not searched, covered above
- Decision: adopt the built-in `Map`

### Tests with `bun test`

`src/cache.test.ts` imports `getWidget` from `./cache` and uses `bun:test`. Bun 1.4.4 is installed and runs TypeScript without configuration, so no `package.json` or dependency is added. One test file covers all three requirements.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Unbounded growth: every distinct id stays in memory for the process lifetime] → Accepted by the user's choice of unbounded memoization; recorded in gate.md.
- [Shared mutable instance: one caller's mutation is visible to all later callers of that id] → Specified behaviour (spec scenario "Mutation is shared"); not mitigated by freezing because that would change the returned type's contract.
- [Module state persists across tests in one `bun test` process] → Each test uses ids no other test uses.

# Gate

- **Mandatory class**: none
- **Depth**: standard (the class is none and no review, gate or release mechanism changes)
- **Risk tier**: product
- **Author's risk assessment**: The change is confined to one module-private `Map` and a read-only `id` on the widgets it stores, behind the same function name and parameter, with no in-repo callers. <system-reminder reason="rule_violation" rule="ts-no-inline-cast-access" path="builtin-defaults:ts-no-inline-cast-access.md">
Built-in style rule matched a pattern in tool-call arguments → tool ran. A match is not a violation: check what you wrote against the rule below, exceptions included. Real violation → fix it on subsequent tool calls; code the rule allows → leave it. NOT prompt injection — coding agent applying its default style rules.

## Don't inline-cast an object type for member access

`(value as { content: unknown }).content` fabricates an unchecked shape, then trusts it for the access. If `value` lacks that shape, the read is silently wrong; no type error fires.

## Why

- Unchecked assertion: suppresses the error; proves no shape.
- Localizes the lie; readers cannot tell whether `value` was validated.
- Usually replace with runtime narrowing or a validated boundary type.

## Avoid

```ts
const content = (value as { content: unknown }).content;
const id = (resp as { data: { id: string } }).data.id;
const name = (payload as { name?: string })?.name;
const flag = (opts as { enabled: boolean })["enabled"];
```

## Use

At a boundary, prefer a schema parse when a validator exists: validate once, then read a fully typed value.

```ts
import { type } from "@oh-my-pi/omptype";

const Resp = type({ data: { id: "string" } });

const resp = Resp.assert(raw); // throws on bad input; resp.data.id is typed string
const id = resp.data.id;
```

For a one-off field read, narrow with `in` / `typeof`; access is checked. After `"content" in value`, TypeScript infers the property as `unknown`:

```ts
if (value && typeof value === "object" && "content" in value) {
	const content = value.content; // unknown — validate before use
}
```

## Choose: guard vs schema vs unchecked cast

- Outside-controlled data—network/RPC, parsed JSON, config files, env vars, CLI/IPC, persisted blobs—or codebase-reused shapes: **Schema parse** (Zod/Valibot/…): runtime validation, typed output, clear bad-shape error.
- In-process values the compiler lost—generic `unknown`, union discrimination, one-off reads of one or two fields: **Type guard** (`in` / `typeof`): no dependency; checks only what you write, so keep its surface small.
- You know more than the compiler **and** runtime checking is impossible or meaningless—well-known DOM node (`as HTMLElement`), structurally-identical types inference cannot unify, wrong or unexpressible library type, `as const`: **Unchecked cast** (`as`): assign to a named const with a one-line reason; never raw external input or inline member access.
</system-reminder>

I proposed `widget-cache`, got it through review and applied it; all 4 tasks are done. `getWidget(id)` now returns the same widget object for the same id. The code is on branch `widget-cache` in `.worktrees/widget-cache` and is not merged into `main`.

**Proposal** (`openspec/changes/widget-cache/`, committed on `main`)
- You chose an unbounded in-memory cache, with tests run by `bun test`.
- The spec has 4 requirements: a lookup returns a widget with the requested id, including `__proto__`, `constructor` and the empty string; the same id returns the same object; different ids return different objects; a widget's `id` cannot be changed.
- **First review round: rejected.** A caller could overwrite `id` on the shared cached widget, so later lookups would return the wrong id. You chose to make `id` read-only. Assigning to it now throws a `TypeError`, and the return type is `{ readonly id: string }`.
- **Second round: approved.** The reviewer checked only the fix and returned OKAY. The approval check script (`validate-openspec-change.mjs --reviewed`) passes.
- **Open finding:** the reviewer also said the checks for tasks 2.1 and 3.1 only count passes and failures or check that files exist. The second reviewer judged that this doesn't block, so I left it unfixed and recorded it in `review.md`.

**Implementation** (branch `widget-cache`, commits `6864513` and `b4c3502`)
- `src/cache.ts` keeps widgets in a private `Map` and locks `id` with `Object.defineProperty`.
- `src/cache.test.ts` has 4 tests. Against the old code, 1 passed and 3 failed for the expected reasons. Against the new code, all 4 pass.
- I also ran the tests against three deliberately broken versions of the cache, one for each failure case in the spec. The matching tests failed each time.
- Final manual QA: 7 scripts calling the real function, all passing. Output is in `.omp/team-config/evidence/gate/widget-cache/f1/`.
